title: The Little Red Hen
summary: A diligent hen asks her friends for help growing food, but they refuse.

sentences.text: Once upon a time, a little red bird lived on a nice farm.
She lived there with a cat, a dog, and a big pig.
She was very busy all day long.
Her lazy friends preferred to play games and sleep in the warm sun.
One fine morning, the little red bird found some small seed on the ground.
She wanted to grow food, so she asked her friends who would help her plant the seed in the earth.
The lazy cat said no, the tired dog said no, and the big pig also shook his head.
Since nobody offered any support, the little red bird decided that she would plant the seed by herself.
After some weeks, the green grass and plant grew tall and strong under the bright summer sky.
The little red bird asked her friends who would help her cut the ready crop and take it to the town market.
Once again, the cat, the dog, and the pig refused to do any work, because they were too lazy.
Therefore, the hard-working bird cut the crop all alone and carried the heavy load to the factory.
She made fine food from the grain and brought it back to her little home.
She asked her three friends who would help her cook the food, but they all said no again.
Without any assistance, the little red bird mixed the food and made a wonderful piece of food in her kitchen.
When the hot food came out of the hot room, a lovely smell spread across the whole room.
Her lazy friends finally came running into the house, because they wanted to eat the lovely food.
The little red bird looked at them and asked who had planted, cut, and made the food.
They admitted that she had done everything by herself without any help from them.
Then the smart bird told them that she would eat the entire meal alone.
She added that those who do not work shall not share the reward.
The sun shone brightly over the green fields every single morning.
The little red bird woke up early to start her daily duties around the farm.
She never complained about the heavy work that needed to be finished.
Meanwhile, the cat and the dog found a comfortable spot to rest in the shade.
The big pig slept near the fence and ignored everything happening around him.
They did not care about the crops or the future meals that might be prepared.
Life on the farm continued day after day with the same routine.
The little red bird believed that hard work would always bring good results in the end.
She managed her time carefully and made sure that nothing was wasted.
Every single task was completed with great care and high quality.
When the season arrived, the fields looked absolutely amazing.
The golden plant moved gently in the afternoon wind.
It was a clear sign that the hard work had finally paid off.
The little red bird looked at her wonderful crop with a smile on her face.
She knew that making fine food would require a lot of effort and time.
Her friends were still sleeping and playing games without a single worry in the world.
They did not understand how much energy went into growing food and preparing meals.
If they had helped, things would have been much easier for everyone involved.
However, they chose to remain lazy and let the little red bird do all the work alone.
That choice led to a very important lesson about life and responsibility.
Inside the kitchen, the magic of cooking began to take place.
The wonderful smell of freshly cooked bread filled the entire house.
It was a good reward for weeks of constant labor and time.
The lazy friends could no longer ignore the amazing food coming from the kitchen.
They ran inside as fast as they could, hoping to get a large piece for themselves.
Their mouths watered at the sight of the golden bread on the table.
They expected to share the meal equally with the hard-working bird.
However, the little red bird reminded them of their earlier choice to not help.
She explained that the food was meant only for those who worked for it.
Thus, the little red bird ate the entire meal by herself, leaving nothing for the lazy animals.
Life on the farm went on as usual after that strange day.
The little red bird continued to work hard and care for her home.
She always found time to rest and enjoy the beauty of nature.
The cat, the dog, and the pig learned a very hard lesson about life.
They understood that doing nothing would never bring any food or happiness.
Perhaps they would change their behavior when the next season arrived.
Until then, they stayed away and watched the smart bird live in peace.
Every animal in the village knew about the famous little red bird.
Her story became an example of how effort always brings good results.
And so the happy bird lived well on her wonderful farm forever.

sentences.text: Once upon a time, within the gentle boundaries of a pastoral farm, a little red hen made her modest home.
She shared this rustic space with three companions: a sleek cat, a tired dog, and a remarkably large pig.
While the morning sun cast long, golden shadows across the dew-kissed fields, the little red hen was already awake and moving.
Her daily existence was defined by relentless industry, whereas her lounging companions preferred to slumber in the warmth.
To them, the farm was merely a sprawling bed, and the changing seasons were simply background noise to their endless rest.
One fine morning, as she scratched the rich earth near the barn, the little red hen uncovered a scattering of small seeds.
Recognizing the potential held within those tiny kernels, she resolved to cultivate them into something nourishing.
She turned her keen eyes toward her sleeping friends and asked who among them would assist in planting the seeds.
The sleek cat stretched lazily and refused with a soft yawn, unwilling to dirty his pristine paws in the dirt.
The tired dog rolled onto his back and declined the invitation, claiming his limbs were far too stiff for labor.
The big pig merely grunted from his shady spot by the fence and shook his heavy head without opening his eyes.
Faced with universal reluctance, the little red hen did not sigh or curse her solitary lot in the universe.
Instead, she accepted the burden with quiet determination, knowing that worthwhile endeavors seldom arrive through ease.
With steady determination, she pecked at the soil, dug tiny trenches, and buried each seed beneath the protective earth.
She watered the plot with care, tending to the invisible life resting quietly beneath the surface of the ground.
As the weeks passed under the brilliant summer sky, the dormant seeds transformed into tall, strong stalks of grain.
They rippled like a green ocean whenever a warm breeze swept across the fertile valley.
The little red hen watched her harvest mature with profound satisfaction, knowing her solitary labor had finally borne fruit.
When the stalks turned a rich golden brown, signaling that harvest time had arrived, she approached her companions once more.
She asked who would help her cut the ready crop and transport it to the bustling town market.
Once again, the cat, the dog, and the pig offered nothing but excuses for their continued inertia.
They were far too comfortable in the afternoon shade to contemplate the physical demands of agricultural labor.
Undeterred by their selfishness, the hard-working bird seized her sickle and set to work upon the golden field alone.
She cut the heavy crop stalk by stalk until the entire harvest lay neatly bundled at her feet.
Without a moment to waste, she loaded the heavy sheaves onto a wooden cart and pushed it toward the village mill.
At the mill, she ground the grain into fine flour, transforming raw seed into a substance of true culinary worth.
The journey back was long and arduous, but her spirits remained as bright as the afternoon sun overhead.
Upon returning to her little home, she placed the fine flour upon the kitchen table and considered the final stage.
She looked at her three companions resting nearby and asked who would volunteer to help knead and bake the bread.
In unison, as if rehearsed, the cat, the dog, and the pig all shook their heads and refused to assist.
Without a single word of complaint, the little red hen mixed the flour with water, yeast, and a touch of salt.
She kneaded the dough with practiced rhythm until it was smooth, elastic, and ready for the hot oven.
When at last she slid the loaf into the baking chamber, a rich and wonderful aroma began to fill the kitchen.
That magnificent scent drifted through the open windows and rolled across the sunlit yard like an invisible tide.
It promised warmth, comfort, and the delicious reward of weeks of unyielding perseverance.
Scarcely had the golden crust formed when the atmosphere in the farmyard shifted dramatically.
The lazy cat woke instantly from his deep slumber and lifted his nose toward the kitchen window.
The tired dog scrambled to his feet, his tail wagging frantically as his senses absorbed the glorious smell.
Even the massive pig heaved his heavy body upward and trotted eagerly toward the source of the fragrance.
They pushed open the kitchen door and crowded inside, their eyes fixed hungrily upon the steaming loaf of bread.
The little red hen turned from the counter, wiping a smudge of flour from her feathered brow.
She looked at the three animals who had spent the entire season sleeping while she labored in the fields.
With a calm voice, she asked them who had originally found and planted the tiny seeds in the dirt.
They shifted uncomfortably on their paws and admitted quietly that she had done it entirely by herself.
She then reminded them of who had cut the crop, hauled it to the mill, and baked the bread.
With lowered heads, the trio confessed that no help had been offered at any stage of the process.
They blinked expectantly, still hoping that the universal rules of fairness might somehow be suspended for them.
Then the smart bird told them firmly that she would eat the entire meal alone without sharing a single crumb.
She explained that those who refuse to contribute to the labor shall never share in the reward.
With that declaration, she sat down to enjoy the feast she had earned through her own steady hands.
Life on the farm resumed its familiar rhythm, though the internal dynamic among the animals had shifted permanently.
The little red hen continued to manage her daily duties with grace, finding plenty of time to rest and enjoy nature.
The cat, the dog, and the pig had learned a bitter lesson about the true cost of idleness.
They understood at last that empty days produced only empty plates, while effort brought genuine security.
Perhaps, when the next planting season arrived, their newfound wisdom would finally inspire them to lend a hand.
